newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks start higher, helped by bonds.
newsitem.headline: French stocks start higher, helped by bonds.

text.p: French shares started higher on Friday, supported by firmness in bonds and the franc, traders said.
But the market would likely stay cautious while waiting for U.S. producer prices and retail sales figures due at 1230 GMT.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 6.25 points or 0.24 percent at 2,614.22 at 0820 GMT, while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 12 at 2,618 from Thursday's close.
Lyonnaise des Eaux, Cie de Suez were both suspended. The companies are expected to announce a merger agreement this evening after their boards meet to approve terms.
The market expects a merger parity of 41 Suez for 20 Lyonnaise shares and a Suez dividend of some 24 francs.
PSA Peugeot Citroen and Renault rose respectively 2.4 percent to 641 francs and 0.68 percent to 147.5, helped by a more optimistic view of European manufacturers after strong Volkswagen sales.
Synthelabo dropped 1.34 percent to 663, running into profit-taking after rising strongly in the week.
Other pharmaceuticals and cosmetics stocks were gainers, with Sanofi up 1.82 percent to 559 and L'Oreal, which owns 57 percent of Synthelabo, 1.35 percent higher at 2,022.
Accor rose 1.21 percent to 835 francs. The stock is considered a cheap valuation and with potential for gains under a restructuring with new chairman Jean-Marc Espalioux.

The market is looking for a 0.6 percent rise in U.S. March retail sales on the headline figure and a 0.4 percent advance in the core data, excluding cars. Producer prices are expected to show no change on the headline.
